description: The rep unilaterally books a time; the customer only backchannels and defers. A later 'get back to you Thursday' is a deadline, not a meeting.

turns.text: I'll put us down for Thursday at 3 to go through the contract redlines.
Mm. I'll have to check with legal on their availability.
Sure. Anything else you need from me before then?
No, I think we're good. I'll get back to you on Thursday either way about the redlines.

decisionMaker.rationale: Legal is consulted about availability only; no approval authority is stated.

evidence.quote: I'll put us down for Thursday at 3 to go through the contract redlines.
I'll have to check with legal on their availability.

nextMeeting.rationale: Only the rep commits to the time. The customer backchannels ('Mm') and defers to legal, so the meeting is plausible but not agreed: TENTATIVE + INDIRECT → ASK. Call date Monday 2026-03-16 → Thursday = 2026-03-19.

notes: Illustrative schema-validation case drafted by Claude. NOT part of the benchmark. 'I'll get back to you on Thursday' is a deadline (sufficiency NONE) and must not be written as a meeting.
